- Base commit: 120M tokens / month (annual billing)

- Renewal uplift cap: 20% default (we can adjust based on smoothing)
- Optional smoothing: 3-month rolling average true-up and a +/- 20% corridor to protect against short spikes

3) Any procurement constraints we should bake into the term sheet (e.g., maximum % increase that CFO will accept)?

If helpful, we can sketch two concrete scenarios (conservative / aggressive) with exact invoices so your finance team can review.

Maya —

Totally reasonable asks. Quick answers:

- Smoothing: we can do a 3-month rolling average true-up with a +/-20% corridor. That means monthly spikes above the corridor are absorbed as overage charges but the 3-month rolling average is used at renewal to adjust the committed tiers. This reduces volatility for budgeting.
- Uplift cap: we can cap renewal price increases at 15% for the first 12 months if Olive agrees to the soft-commit structure (80M guaranteed). We’ll document this in the term sheet.
- Overage ceiling: we can guarantee a per-token ceiling equal to the list price ($0.0022/token) for unexpected spikes; overage would be billed at the next slab until the monthly total, but we won’t exceed $0.0022/token in any single billing month.

Attached is a worked invoice example for a +35% spike month (see slides, tab "Spike Scenario"). In short, with the soft-commit:
- Guaranteed (80M): billed at slab 1 ($0.0018)
- Additional usage 28M (spike): billed starting at slab 2 rate ($0.00145) but capped at $0.0022/token ceiling

Lauren / Marissa — tagging you for any finance/legal considerations before I send a redline.

Thanks,
Dylan

Dylan —

Good plan. A couple of commercial guardrails I recommend before sending to procurement:

1) Make the renewal uplift cap explicit in the commercial summary: "Renewal price increases <= 15% year-over-year for the first renewal period when soft-commit selected."
2) Add an underutilization credit: if actual annualized usage is <75% of committed tokens, apply a 10% credit on the difference applied to the next invoice. This reduces buyer risk.
3) Replace the flat +/-20% corridor with a "usage corridor" tied to a 3-month moving average (e.g., commit +/- 25% of three-month moving average) — more defensible for both sides.
4) Add a hard per-token ceiling in the Master Services Agreement (MSA) Exhibit B: $0.0022/token.

I attached a redlined term sheet (term_sheet_redline_olive.docx) with the language above. Legal will want to tweak but this should address the CFO’s requirement.
